Both MoAs produce rounded mitotic-arrested cells with condensed bright DNA and intense tubulin, so my tub_mean z~15-28 increase was not specific to stabilization — Eg5 monopolar spindles also concentrate tubulin signal. Literature for dossier:
- Eg5 inhibition → monopolar spindles/mitotic arrest: PMID 10542155 (monastrol inhibitor of spindle bipolarity), PMID 19351824 (K858 Eg5 inhibitor induces mitotic arrest/cell death).

reflection.text:
The run correctly detected a strong antimitotic phenotype with huge tubulin intensity/texture increases and condensed, irregular nuclei, but misassigned it to microtubule stabilizers (p 0.80 then 0.71) when truth was Eg5 inhibitors. Verdict: request experiment.

## Reflection

The run correctly detected a strong antimitotic phenotype with huge tubulin intensity/texture increases and condensed, irregular nuclei, but misassigned it to microtubule stabilizers (p 0.80 then 0.71) when truth was Eg5 inhibitors. The atlas was effectively tied at 6/10 stabilizers vs 4/10 Eg5 with near-identical mean similarity, and the review explicitly warned that spindle polarity was unresolved, yet confidence was increased on monotonic tubulin dose-response.

What misled was interpreting well-average tub_mean z=+28.5, tub_std z=+19.7 and tub_glcm_contrast z=+40.2 with Spearman rho=+1.00 as stabilizer-specific bundling. Dense monopolar spindles concentrated in rounded Eg5-arrested mitotics raise the same metrics, and the accompanying nuc_solidity z=-28.3 to -19.1 plus nuc_dna_integrated z up to +19.8 and lower density fit Eg5 arrest equally well (PMID 10542155, PMID 19351824). The low-dose describe_phenotype on w_737bc04593 was the requested discrimination test for spread interphase bundling versus brightness confined to rounded mitotics, but it still returned only a stabilizer candidate without scoring bipolar versus monopolar spindles.

The lesson is that well-average tubulin intensity cannot separate increased polymerization from mitotic spindle compaction, and visual candidates without centrosome/spindle-polarity resolution should not move probability. A tied atlas plus unresolved polarity should have kept Eg5 near 0.5 rather than 0.14-0.20.

What was right:
- Excluded microtubule destabilizers because tub_mean z=+28.5 at 1 uM with dose_response rho=+1.00 showed increased, not lost, tubulin signal.
- Detected mitotic arrest signal from lower density, very low nuc_solidity (z=-28.3 to -19.1) and high nuc_dna_integrated (z up to +19.8).
- Kept Eg5 inhibitors as explicit runner-up because compare_to_reference_atlas was split 6/10 stabilizers vs 4/10 Eg5.
- Down-weighted Aurora kinase inhibitors using nuc_area rho=-1.00 and frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80, opposite the large polyploid expectation.

What was wrong or missed:
- Misread large tub_mean, tub_std and tub_glcm_contrast increases as stabilizer-specific, when Eg5 monopolar spindles in rounded mitotics raise the same well-average measurements.
- Relied on describe_phenotype candidates of Microtubule stabilizers at high dose and at 0.01 uM without ever resolving bipolar bundles versus monopolar rosettes, the discriminator flagged in review.
- Over-calibrated to 0.80 despite atlas tie with mean similarity 0.861 vs 0.867, and claimed tubulin-before-mitosis without separately scoring spread interphase versus rounded mitotic cells at 0.01-0.03 uM.

Proposed next experiment: High-resolution anti-tubulin plus pericentrin/centrosome co-staining to score bipolar bundles versus monopolar Eg5 rosette spindles in arrested mitotics, paired with a cell-free tubulin polymerization assay to test for direct microtubule stabilization.
